EXP–002 / UNITY + C# + ESP32

Physical tokens.
Virtual abilities.

A 2D speedrun platformer where scanning an RFID token changes the player’s movement abilities.

ROLESolo project
STATEIn progress
ORIGINAL BUILD2–3 days / hackathon

The idea

Change one movement rule and a platformer feels different. This project takes that literally: physical tokens select dash, wall jump, gravity flip, or time stop.

The first version was a solo hackathon build. It uses Unity, an ESP32, and an MFRC522 RFID reader. A regular keyboard works too, so the hardware isn’t required to try it.

The technical bit

The interesting boundary is between the thing on the desk and the player on screen. Unity needs to receive the ability choice without being coupled to the RFID reader.

One input path

RFID token↓MFRC522 reader + ESP32↓Bluetooth keyboard input↓Unity ability selection

The ESP32 presents itself as a Bluetooth keyboard. Each recognised token sends a number key. Unity receives ordinary keyboard input, so physical and keyboard controls use the same ability-selection path.

Movement includes acceleration, coyote time, jump buffering, and variable jump height. A timer, local leaderboard, and ghost replay support the speedrun loop.

Still rough

Crush detection, resets, and race/leaderboard edge cases remain in progress. Movement, level readability, the ability HUD, and the browser experience are also being refined.

The repository is ahead of some older exported builds. The project README explains the build setup and current limitations.

Next passes

The next useful addition here is footage showing a physical token changing the game, alongside a closer look at movement and reset behaviour. There’s no stand-in screenshot for that yet.
